title: How is smart delivery expanding beyond traditional package delivery?
summary: Read How is smart delivery expanding beyond traditional package delivery? and explore insights on autonomous delivery, innovation, and Arrive AI updates.
body_markdown:
Delivery is changing. Drones and robots are creating new ways to move packages, while businesses and communities are exploring how these technologies can become part of everyday operations.


But getting a package to its destination is only one part of the delivery process. There also needs to be infrastructure that supports the handoff, provides a secure receiving point, and connects different parts of the delivery journey.


At Arrive AI, we are developing smart delivery infrastructure designed to support this evolving landscape. Through advancements in our AP3 units, technology collaborations, and new industry applications, we are exploring how Arrive Points can work with different delivery methods and serve environments beyond traditional package delivery.


# Advancing the capabilities of Arrive Points


The latest generation of AP3 units features NVIDIA edge computing capabilities, creating new opportunities for how smart delivery infrastructure can process and support technology at the point of delivery.


Edge computing allows certain computing tasks to happen closer to where data is collected and used, rather than relying entirely on a remote system.


These capabilities open possibilities for applications that can further support the development of the Arrive Point Network. As the technology continues to evolve, computing capabilities at the delivery endpoint may play an increasingly important role in connecting devices, systems, and delivery operations.


AP3 Plus brings edge computing and package recognition to the delivery endpoint.


# Connecting drone delivery with smart infrastructure


Drones are creating new possibilities for moving packages, but successful delivery requires more than reaching a destination. There must also be a reliable way to receive the package.


Arrive AI is working with Modovolo to develop precision drone delivery technology designed to interact with Arrive Points.


The collaboration focuses on bringing drone delivery and smart delivery infrastructure together. By connecting the delivery vehicle with a designated receiving point, this approach explores how packages can move from the air to a secure endpoint.


This development is part of a broader effort to make Arrive Points compatible with different delivery methods, helping build an infrastructure network that can support the changing needs of delivery.


# Exploring how robots can interact with Arrive Points


Robotics is another area creating opportunities for the future of delivery.


Through a collaboration with Purdue University’s Institute for Control, Optimization and Networks (ICON), Arrive AI is exploring how humanoid and quadruped robots can interact with Arrive Points.


This work provides an opportunity to study how different types of robots could participate in delivery processes and connect with secure receiving infrastructure.


As robotics technology advances, the ability to coordinate the movement of packages with a reliable receiving point could become an important part of more connected delivery systems.


# Bringing smart delivery into golf and hospitality


Smart delivery infrastructure can also serve environments beyond traditional residential, commercial, and logistics settings.


Arrive AI is testing a smaller Arrive Point configuration designed for golf and hospitality applications.


The company has explored different Arrive Point configurations, including mobile, balcony mounted, mini, and multifamily options. The smaller configuration is being developed with the needs of golf and hospitality environments in mind.


The first unit configured for this application is being prepared for deployment.


This work demonstrates how smart delivery infrastructure can be adapted to different settings, where convenient and secure handoffs can support the needs of guests, staff, and operations.


Concept illustration of how drone delivery and Arrive Points could support food, beverage, and merchandise orders on a golf course.


# Expanding enterprise opportunities in healthcare and manufacturing


Healthcare and manufacturing are also important areas of opportunity for smart delivery infrastructure.


Arrive AI is working with DXC to introduce its technology to large organizations in these sectors. Through presentations and business introductions, the collaboration is creating opportunities to explore how Arrive Points could support delivery operations in different enterprise environments.


These conversations are an important step in identifying potential applications for secure, connected delivery infrastructure across industries.


# Why infrastructure matters as delivery evolves


Drones and robots may change how packages move, but the delivery process does not end when a vehicle reaches its destination.


Packages still need to be received, secured, and transferred to the right person or location. Without infrastructure to support that final handoff, new delivery methods may face limitations as they expand into more environments.


This is where smart delivery infrastructure becomes important.


Arrive AI is developing the Arrive Point Network to support different delivery methods and provide a connected receiving point for packages. Whether a delivery arrives through a traditional courier, drone, or robot, the receiving infrastructure remains an essential part of the process.


The opportunity is not simply to develop new ways to move packages. It is to create the infrastructure that helps connect those delivery methods with the places and people receiving them.


# Building for the future of smart delivery


The future of delivery will involve more than one type of vehicle or technology. Drones, robots, traditional couriers, and other delivery methods will need systems that allow them to work within a connected network.


From expanding AP3 capabilities to developing drone and robotics integrations and exploring new applications in golf, hospitality, healthcare, and manufacturing, Arrive AI is working to advance the infrastructure behind this changing delivery landscape.


As delivery technology continues to evolve, Arrive AI is focused on an essential part of the process: making the final handoff more connected, secure, and accessible.
